correctness.rationale: For all integers \(p\ge3,q\ge2\), connectedness after two deletions is established. Spectral decomposition yields exact incidence quadratic forms; Woodbury yields the rank-two trace update. Seven exhaustive automorphism classes produce rational functions. Positive-denominator, positive-coefficient certificates establish A>B,C and B>D,E,F,G; the B-C difference has one positive root between consecutive integers \(R_p\) and \(R_p+1\), precluding ties. Exact symbolic checker and 80 independent rational matrix inverse calculations were replayed; finite examples corroborate an analytic all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The literature search was statement- and implication-based, including exact same split graph class and more general graph deletion frameworks. Complete split intact-index bounds (Yang 2014) and near-complete deletion ordering (Xu et al. 2016) cover background and restricted cases, whereas general edge-defect calculation (Tamura 2026) does not state the specific orbit comparison and cubic runner-up threshold. value.rationale: This class has two distinct vertex types and realistic worst two-link failure modes. The theorem completely distinguishes worst and runner-up pairs for every nontrivial \(p\ge3,q\ge2\), with explicit numbers of maximizing pairs. The cubic changeover \(q=p^3-3p^2+p+1\) is an exact, nonobvious design boundary between incident and disjoint failure types, with substantive application in network resistance robustness and a complete structural classification rather than a routine isolated calculation.
